sections.h2: Why do houses in Fairborn sell on a different clock than other Dayton suburbs?
sections.html:
Fairborn's buyer pool follows Wright State University and the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base payroll, so demand shifts with academic calendars and military assignments. A seller who needs a closing date before the next move can choose a cash buyer, a listing, or a by-owner sale, and the route should fit the house's condition.

  • Listing: reaches the widest group of buyers and waits on financing and appraisal.
  • By owner: lets you keep the agent's fee, with every showing and form on your plate.
  • Cash purchase: suits homes with worn systems, rental turnover problems or an estate behind them, because the buyer purchases the house as it is.

Fairborn is a suburb of Dayton in the Dayton metropolitan area, and the county seat is Xenia. The Greene County Auditor handles the deed transfer for a Fairborn sale.

Wright State enrolls nearly 12,000 undergraduate and graduate students, and the median resident of Fairborn was 34.0 years old at the 2020 census, well below the other cities in this guide. That younger population shapes which homes move easily and which rentals turn over often.

sections.h2: How did Fairborn become one city out of two villages?
sections.html:
Fairborn is a combined name made from Fairfield and Osborn, the two villages that merged under a charter signed on January 1, 1950, with incorporation on August 1, 1950. Fairfield was founded in 1816 and Osborn in 1850, the latter named for a railroad superintendent whose line the village welcomed after Fairfield refused it.

After the Great Dayton Flood of 1913, the state created a conservation district here, and Huffman Dam went up on the Mad River in the 1920s. About 200 Osborn houses were moved by mules and tractors, and many still stand in the Historic Osborn District. From 1950 to 1970 the city grew to six times its former size, passing Xenia as the most populous city in Greene County, largely on the strength of the nearby Air Force base. Interstate 675, finished in 1987, now carries traffic along the east side of town.

Fairborn covers 14.725 square miles, with 8.864 square miles of the land zoned residential. The city manages 773.2 acres of parks, preserves and cemeteries, and Oakes Quarry Park is among its best known. Fairborn City Schools opened a new primary school in 2020, a new intermediate school in 2022 and a new high school in 2024, and the middle school is Fairborn Baker Middle School. Southwestern Portland Cement once ran the largest factory in the city, mining the locally exposed Brassfield Formation, and the Mercer Log House, 5/3 Commons, Central Park and the Wright Brothers Huffman Prairie Bikeway are among the places buyers hear about.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Fairborn homes and incomes?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts estimates Fairborn's population at 35,754 on July 1, 2025, a 3.7 percent rise from the 2020 base, which makes it the fastest growing of the four cities in this guide. The 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner occupied home is $175,000, and 51.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.

  • Median gross rent: $977
  • Households: 15,911, averaging 2.14 people
  • Median household income: $61,751
  • Per capita income: $37,921
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 30.2 percent
  • Average commute: 21.2 minutes
  • Foreign born residents: 5.3 percent
  • Persons in poverty: 13.7 percent

The 2020 census counted 34,510 people in 15,601 households and 16,707 housing units. The city lists Wright State University as its largest employer at 2,300 workers, followed by Morris Home Furnishings at 443, Peerless Technologies at 300 and Ali Industries at 282. Fairborn levies a 2.0 percent income tax plus a 0.5 percent school district tax, which a move out of town may change.

sections.h2: Which Fairborn city rules matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
Fairborn enforces a property maintenance code found in Part Thirteen, Title Five of its codified ordinances. It covers siding, broken windows, gutters, roofs, walls, foundations, sidewalks, sheds, garages, fences and debris, and it also reaches stored materials and vehicles parked in the yard. A violation notice on your address can complicate a closing, so deal with it early.

  • Reports and complaints: the city's 24 hour line is 937-318-1605. Illegally parked vehicles and noise go to the Police non-emergency line, 937-754-3000.
  • Assessments: the Finance Department has an Assessment Inquiry Form so a buyer or seller can ask whether special assessments are attached to a parcel.
  • Abandoned property: the Property Maintenance Division asks neighbors to help identify vacant, unsecured buildings.

Fairborn also hosts the disaster training facility known as Calamityville, and growth since the late 1980s has run at a moderate pace, with neighboring Beavercreek now larger.

sections.h2: How does the Greene County Auditor handle a Fairborn deed?
sections.html:
Fairborn lies in Greene County, so the Greene County Auditor's office transfers the deed and charges the transfer and conveyance fees. The Real Estate Department can be reached at (937) 562-5072 and maintains records on more than 73,000 parcels.

Greene County Auditor deed transfer requirements, as published by the county
RequirementDetail
Statement of valueDTE 100 or DTE 100 (EX) with the deed
Grantor nameMust read as it did on the previous deed
Map departmentApproves and initials the deed before the Auditor sees it
SignatureGrantor signs, and the deed is notarized
Conveyance fee$2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price
Parcel transfer fee$0.50 per parcel

The Auditor's website carries a conveyance fee calculator, so ask your title company to run it. State law adds one more duty: Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires a signed disclosure form for homes with one to four units. A buyer who receives the form after signing may rescind within three business days, and no later than the earlier of 30 days after acceptance or closing.

sections.h2: Is a quick sale the better call for a Fairborn rental or inherited house?
sections.html:
A quick sale often fits a rental with a turnover problem or an inherited house with a distant owner. The state disclosure statute exempts a seller who inherited the property and did not live in it during the prior year, which removes one task from the list.

Before you sign with anyone, gather these items:

  • A written offer showing the price, the closing date and who pays each fee.
  • Proof of funds from a cash buyer, or a lender's letter from a financed one.
  • The Greene County Auditor's conveyance figure, which your title company can run through the county calculator.
  • Any city violation notice, assessment inquiry response or tenant lease that touches the address.

faqs.q: What does the Greene County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The county publishes a conveyance fee of $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price and $0.50 per parcel. Use the county's conveyance fee calculator for your actual figure.

faqs.q: Whom do I call about a property maintenance problem in Fairborn?
faqs.a: Call the city's 24 hour hotline at 937-318-1605. Parking and noise complaints go to the Fairborn Police Department non-emergency line at 937-754-3000.

faqs.q: Can a Fairborn buyer find out about assessments on a parcel?
faqs.a: Yes. The Finance Department accepts an Assessment Inquiry Form from people considering a purchase, and a representative responds with the assessment details.

faqs.q: Is the Fairborn income tax rate the same after a move out of the city?
faqs.a: No. The city levies a 2.0 percent income tax and a 0.5 percent school district tax on residents, so a move to another municipality can change what you owe. Ask a tax preparer about your situation.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Fairborn?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a 2020 to 2024 median of $175,000 for owner occupied homes in Fairborn. Your house may sit above or below that figure, depending on its condition, size and distance from the campus and the base, so check recent nearby sales and ask for more than one offer.
